name: Three-pillar cinematic drone (layering, movement, FX): wavetable VCO pair + self-feedback delay loop + granular layer, effects after filters with master low-cut as tension control
goal: Build a cinematic drone from three layers and three pillars: (1) a wavetable VCO pair (second one octave down on a slowly volume-modulated VCA) through a low-pass with slow LFO on table position; (2) a self-oscillating feedback loop from a granular/delay processor with no input (feedback raised until it sings, any re-patched input attenuated) through its own resonant low-pass; (3) a granular layer recording 2–3 random sources, with intensity, short grain length for lo-fi, quantized pitch randomization, follow/auto-scan, overdub, S&H choosing layers and an LFO on grain length — all summed through a master filter BEFORE a shimmer reverb so resonance in the low band excites the reverb, using the filter's low cut/cutoff as the scene's tension control (more highs = tension, more lows = suspense).

source.title: Ep. 04 | How to Build Powerful Cinematic Drone Sounds (Modular Synth Sound Design)

prerequisites: Wavetable oscillators, VCAs, LFOs, resonant low-pass filters
Delay/granular processor that can self-feedback, granular sampler with record/overdub
Shimmer reverb, delay (Web Audio: DelayNode feedback loops with gain < 1 plus limiter, implementation note)

outputs.name: cinematic_drone
outputs.description: Layered, moving drone bed with tension control

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Never leave a feedback loop unattenuated — you lose control.
Presenter worked mono into stereo FX at the end; stereo grains are better if available.
Gear-specific modules are mapped to generic functions only.

steps.action: Layer 1: two wavetable VCOs on separate VCA channels, VCO2 one octave below; slowly modulate VCO2's level so the sub appears sometimes; low-pass to cut buzzy harmonics.
steps.expect: Already a usable drone with reverb

steps.action: Movement on layer 1: very slow LFO on wavetable position/axis; optionally resonance/drive/wave-shaper for more harmonics.

Layer 2 (feedback loop): with no input, raise the processor's feedback until it starts self-generating; keep delay lines close; run it into its own resonant low-pass; if feeding output back to input, attenuate it first and lower input gain.
steps.expect: Noisy, unpredictable tonal bed; sub-octave/tone controls shape it

steps.action: Layer 3 (granular): record 2–3 different short sources (even a click or mic sound) as layers; set intensity (grain count), short grain length for lo-fi, quantized pitch randomization; use follow mode to auto-scan through the recording, forward or reverse; overdub (e.g. whistling) for new tones.
steps.expect: Three tonal strata: high ethereal, mid, sub

steps.action: Movement on layer 3: sample-and-hold selects which recorded layer plays; an LFO modulates grain length.
Sum layers, then a master low-pass with resonance BEFORE shimmer reverb and delay so resonant low harmonics feed the reverb.
steps.expect: Harmonic correlation in the low band; shimmer adds high overtones from them

steps.action: Use the master filter's low cut / cutoff as the tension control: more high frequencies = tension ('something is coming'), lows = suspense; choose reverb type for mood; end a scene by pulling inputs out and leaving a little wet.

verification: Muting each layer changes the bed distinctly (tone/noise/texture).
Raising master cutoff increases perceived tension; lowering it darkens without stopping.
Feedback layer stays bounded (no runaway) over a 1-minute hold.
